sources.entry: RustCast - Blazingly fast, customisable multi tool, application launcher

summary.one_liner: RustCast is a Rust-based, macOS popup launcher for opening apps and running utilities, similar in purpose to Raycast, which the author says is no longer maintained.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a popup launcher that autoloads installed apps and lets you search them. Built-in features listed as finished include a calculator, unit conversions, emoji search, file search, clipboard history (opened by typing `cbhist`), and a `randomvar` command that generates a number from 0 to 100. It can also Google a query when you end it with `?`, control Spotify, and pass variables into custom shell scripts. Appearance options include customisable themes and colours, blur or transparent backgrounds, tray icons, and image icons next to results. Navigation uses arrow keys or CTRL n/p, and the config lives at `~/.config/rustcast/config.toml`. The planned list includes popup note-taking, a hyperkey, and plugin support, which is only partially implemented. Cross-platform support is marked as not planned.
use_cases: launch installed macOS apps by typing their name
search files from a popup launcher
run quick calculations and unit conversions
run custom shell scripts from a launcher
free alternative to Raycast on macOS
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the dmg from the GitHub releases page
Edit ~/.config/rustcast/config.toml to customise (RustCast creates a default config on first run)
stack: mdfind (used for file search, per README credits)
notable: Free, open-source Raycast-style launcher written in Rust
Built-in clipboard history, calculator, unit conversion, and emoji search
Customisable themes, colours, and blur or transparent background
Vim-style CTRL n/p navigation for results
Shell script integration with variables passed in
caveats: The README says the project is no longer maintained.
macOS only; cross-platform support is explicitly not planned.
Plugin support is only partially implemented and the config docs link is empty in the README.
